parole.testo: From Latin cainito, from Spanish caimito, from Lokono.

parole.significato: Any long marking, dark or bright, on a planet or moon's surface.
parole.testo: From Latin līnea (“line, thread”), via Spanish línea in reference to the unit of length, from līnum (“flax”). Doublet of ligne; related to line.

parole.significato: Of, pertaining to, resembling, or connected with a peninsula or peninsulas.
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Latin paenīnsulāris. By surface analysis, peninsula + -ar. In the historical sense borrowed from Spanish peninsular.
Originally as a calque or translation of various Latin or Spanish terms.

parole.significato: Of or relating to the Vascons, a people of ancient Iberia, thought to be the ancestors of the Basque.
parole.testo: Derived from Latin Vascones; the name may have originally been borrowed through Spanish vascón, vasco. Doublet of Gascon.
